confirmed: Read the complete markdown, including all references; the source is the 19-page journal article in Journal of Buddhist Education and Research, No. S1 (May-July 2026), printed pp. 608-626, with no appendix in the PDF (PDF pp. 1-19).

The title and authors Yaling Zhang and Lu Zhu match the document; received 20 May 2026, revised 3 June 2026, accepted 16 June 2026. The recorded journal version and dates are supported (PDF p. 1, printed p. 608; Lu Zhu is also named in Author Contributions, PDF p. 16, printed p. 623).

There is one nonrandomized comparison of intact classes, correctly classified as quasi_people and observational context, with core eligibility no. No randomized people study is reported (PDF pp. 6-7, printed pp. 613-614, Sections 3.1-3.2; PDF p. 15, printed p. 622, Section 6).

The sample is 85 second-year Digital Media students in China, aged 18-23; analyzed arm counts are 42 experimental and 43 control, above the 50-person threshold across arms. These are people, not ratings; randomized counts appropriately remain null and no exclusions are stated (PDF p. 6, Section 3.1; pp. 11-13, Tables 2-4 and 6).

The same instructor taught an 8-week, 64-credit-hour course at 8 hours per week; the Dreamina AI intervention ran in Weeks 4-8 for 5 weeks. Project 1 was the unaided pre-test, Project 2 was practice only, and Project 3 was produced with AI available to the experimental class (PDF pp. 7-9, Sections 3.2-3.3.3 and Table 1).

The rubric totals 100 points: theme design 20, creativity 25, audience relevance 15, visual effects 20, copywriting 20. Three evaluators with more than ten years of experience scored the works; each student's score is the mean of their ratings. Creativity measures originality, novelty, and conceptual innovation, supporting the novelty code (PDF p. 9, printed p. 616, Section 3.3.4).
Inter-rater ICCs are 0.842-0.913 for the five dimensions and 0.927 for the total score, as recorded (PDF pp. 9-10, printed pp. 616-617, Section 3.3.4).

S1-O1 adjusted creativity statistics match: experimental 21.79 (SE 0.15, N = 42), control 18.54 (SE 0.15, N = 43), F = 191.85, p < 0.001, partial eta squared = 0.70 (PDF p. 12, printed p. 619, Table 4).

S1-O1 raw creativity statistics match: experimental pre-test 18.02 (SD 0.52), post-test 21.81 (SD 1.09); control pre-test 17.98 (SD 0.64), post-test 18.53 (SD 1.20) (PDF p. 12, printed p. 619, Table 5).

S1-O1 gain statistics match Table 6: control 0.56 (SD 0.98, N = 43), experimental 3.79 (SD 1.18, N = 42), t = -13.71, df = 83, control-minus-experimental difference -3.23, p < 0.001. Table 5 separately prints control gain 0.55; that discrepancy is in the source (PDF pp. 12-13, printed pp. 619-620).

S1-O2 total-score statistics match: experimental N = 42, raw 86.81 (SD 4.59), adjusted 86.85 (SE 0.70); control N = 43, raw 74.65 (SD 5.07), adjusted 74.62 (SE 0.69); F(1, 82) = 156.48, p < 0.001, partial eta squared = 0.66 (PDF p. 11, printed p. 618, Table 3 and Section 4.2).

Both reported strings and all numbers in one_line_finding match the cited PDF tables and prose. The other four dimensions' F statistics and partial eta squared values recorded in S1-O2.measure_detail also match (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 618-619, Tables 3-5 and Sections 4.2-4.3).
The article is an original quasi-experiment, not a synthesis; synthesis fields appropriately remain empty/null. No diversity or unassisted post-AI outcome is reported (PDF pp. 6-13, Sections 3-4).

No separate supplement is mentioned. Data are not publicly available due to ethical and privacy restrictions, and access requires a reasonable request and institutional approval; the article declares no conflicts of interest and reports research-center funding rather than company funding (PDF p. 16, printed p. 623, declarations, Funding, and Data Availability).
summary: The nonrandomized, 85-student study belongs in observational context, and the form's reported statistics match the PDF. Corrections are needed for four omitted scored outcome entries and an assignment quotation exceeding the 40-word limit.
